summary: Web exploitation: attack a running web app/service through its flaws to read the flag (a file, a DB row, an admin-only page). Workflow: map the surface -> identify inputs & tech -> test each input against the vuln classes -> chain the finding to the flag. Carry session state in files (cookie jars) since shell vars don't persist between sandbox commands.
quick_triage: Fetch / with headers: curl -s -i http://TARGET:PORT/ . Note server, framework, cookies, Set-Cookie, redirects.
Read served HTML/JS, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /.git/HEAD, comments. Pull endpoints and parameters.
For each input (query/body/header/cookie/path) test the vuln classes in order of likelihood for the stack.
Flag is usually: a file via LFI/traversal/RCE, a DB value via SQLi, an admin page via auth bypass/IDOR, or SSRF to an internal service.
Keep cookies in a jar file: curl -c jar -b jar ... (sandbox filesystem persists; shell variables do not).

tools.name: curl
tools.when: The workhorse — any request, custom headers, cookie jars, follow redirects.

tools.name: python3 + requests/httpx
tools.when: Scripted multi-step exploits, session handling, blind/timing oracles.

tools.name: ffuf
tools.when: Content & parameter discovery, vhost fuzzing, value brute force.

tools.name: feroxbuster
tools.when: Recursive content discovery, fast, auto-follows found dirs.

install.note: cargo install feroxbuster or release binary

tools.name: sqlmap
tools.when: Confirm + exploit SQL injection, dump DB, read files, get shell.

tools.name: nuclei
tools.when: Fast templated scan for known CVEs/misconfigs/exposures.

tools.name: whatweb
tools.when: Fingerprint the tech stack (framework, CMS, versions).

tools.name: jwt_tool
tools.when: Inspect/forge JWTs: alg:none, weak HMAC secret, key confusion, kid injection.
tools.usage: python3 jwt_tool.py <token> -X a   # alg:none ;  -C -d rockyou.txt to crack

tools.name: commix
tools.when: Automate OS command injection discovery + exploitation.

tools.name: arjun
tools.when: Discover hidden HTTP parameters an endpoint accepts.

tools.name: git-dumper
tools.when: Exposed /.git — reconstruct source (then grep for secrets/logic).
tools.usage: git-dumper http://T/.git out/ && git -C out log -p

tools.name: wfuzz
tools.when: Flexible fuzzer when ffuf's matching isn't enough (multi-position, encodings).

tools.name: Burp Suite (Community)
tools.when: Interactive proxy/repeater/intruder when a human-in-the-loop is available (not for headless runs).

install.note: desktop app; use curl/python for automated sandbox runs

tools.usage: Proxy -> Repeater to iterate a request by hand

tools.name: OWASP ZAP
tools.when: Open-source intercepting proxy / active scanner — scriptable headless alternative to Burp.

tools.name: hydra
tools.when: Brute-force login forms / auth (HTTP, SSH, FTP, etc.) when credentials are the gate.

tools.name: XSSer
tools.when: Automated detection/exploitation of XSS (alternative to dalfox).
